newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian car maker Astra seen as takeover target.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian car maker Astra seen as takeover target.

text.p: Indonesia's largest vehicle manufacturer, Astra International, could be the target of a takeover bid with huge block buying orders pushed through this week, brokers said on Wednesday.

Brokers said purchase orders for 54 million shares, around five percent of the company's equity, were booked on Monday and Tuesday, sending the share's local price to a year-high of 3,775 rupiah by Wednesday afternoon.
The share, which closed at 2,625 rupiah on September 16, has been steadily rising since rumours surfaced early last week that a takeover bid was in the works.
Brokers said most of the buy orders emanated from Singapore and added it was likely that a syndicate of Indonesian tycoons was preparing to gain a controlling stake in the company.

"There is continuing large-scale buying out of Singapore," said the head of a foreign brokerage firm in Jakarta. "We believe it's a syndicate of two or three Indonesian businessmen, probably headed by Putra Sampoerna."

Sampoerna, who controls Indonesian tobacco giant PT Hanjaya Mandala Sampoerna, was in the news last month after he announced a conditional takeover for Singapore-listed trading and telecommunications company Transmarco Holdings
An aide confirmed Putra Sampoerna had bought some shares in Astra this week, but said she did not have details of the amount involved or the price.

Analysts said Astra was a good target for a takeover since its holdings were widely scattered, with the largest held by Delta Mutika, a company controlled by Indonesian businessman Prajogo Pangestu, with a 10.68 percent stake.
Toyota Motor Corp holds the next-largest stake at 8.26 percent. The rest is divided among a clutch of Indonesian business houses.
"We feel that a 18-20 percent stake will be enough to control the company," the brokerage head said, adding that Pangestu was reported to be prepared to sell his stake to the syndicate.
Other brokers said the syndicate could also include members of President Suharto's family, possibly his youngest son, Hutomo Mandala Putra, also known as Tommy.
Mandala Putra was awarded the sole right to manufacture Indonesia's national car earlier this year with tax and tariff breaks subject to meeting local content requirements.
He has set up a joint venture with Kia Motors of South Korea to manufacture 1,600 cc sedans, which were launched in July.

Analysts said Astra's production and distribution network would come in handy for Timor Putra Nasional, the company controlled by Mandala Putra, and said it was likely other members of the syndicate could hive off other divisions.

"If Tommy Suharto is serious about his national car, the most cost-effective way of getting a local component manufacturing base is to buy a stake in Astra," said an analyst from a leading Jakarta brokerage.
But he added that Toyota would probably oppose any link with a company which has a South Korean rival for a partner.

A senior official at Astra said he was not aware who was buying into the company. He said no intimation had been received of block share transfers, although the capital markets supervisory board Bapepam would have to be informed if any one holding exceeded five percent.
"But I think it is unlikely Bapepam will be involved since most of the buying would have been done through nominees," he added.
